scheme_name: Production of Tiatr in Villages/Urban Areas/Educational Institutions
description:
The "Production of Tiatr in Villages/Urban Areas/Educational Institutions" scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of Goa to promote the traditional Goan theatrical art form known as Tiatr. 

Tiatr is a unique form of musical theatre that has its roots in the Portuguese influence on Goan culture. 

The scheme was officially launched on 1st January 2020. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to encourage the production of Tiatr by providing financial assistance to individuals and groups involved in this art form. 

The government aims to preserve and promote the cultural heritage of Goa through Tiatr. 

The scheme also seeks to enhance the skills of local artists and provide them with a platform to showcase their talents. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to support at least 50 Tiatr productions annually. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹1 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2020-2021. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance of up to ₹2 lakh is provided for each Tiatr production. 

The assistance is intended to cover expenses related to staging, costumes, sets, and other production costs. 

The scheme is open to both individuals and groups, including educational institutions that wish to produce Tiatr. 

Eligibility criteria for applicants include being a resident of Goa. 

Applicants must also demonstrate a genuine interest in promoting Tiatr and must provide a detailed proposal for their production. 

There are no specific age limits for applicants under this scheme. 

However, groups must consist of a minimum of 10 members to qualify for assistance. 

Educational institutions must be recognized by the Government of Goa to be eligible for funding. 

The application process involves submitting a proposal to the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

The proposal must include details such as the script, cast, crew, and a budget breakdown. 

Applicants are required to submit a copy of their identity proof and address proof along with the proposal. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee formed by the Directorate of Art and Culture. 

The committee evaluates the proposals based on creativity, feasibility, and the potential impact on promoting Tiatr. 

Successful applicants will receive the financial assistance in two installments. 

The first installment of 50% is released upon approval of the proposal. 

The second installment is released after the successful completion of the production and submission of a performance report. 

The timeline for submitting applications is generally open throughout the year. 

However, it is advisable for applicants to submit their proposals at least three months prior to the intended date of the production. 

The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

The contact details for the Directorate are as follows: 

Directorate of Art and Culture, 

Mahatma Gandhi Road, 

Panjim, Goa, 

Pin Code: 403001. 

The phone number for inquiries is +91 832 222 2080. 

The email address for communication is director.artandculture.goa@gmail.com. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from the local community. 

Many artists have reported that the financial assistance has significantly helped in the production quality of Tiatr. 

The government has also organized workshops to train aspiring Tiatr artists. 

These workshops focus on various aspects of production including acting, scriptwriting, and stage management. 

The initiative has led to an increase in the number of Tiatr performances in Goa. 

In 2021, it was reported that over 60 Tiatr productions were staged, surpassing the initial target. 

The scheme has also contributed to the local economy by creating job opportunities for artists, technicians, and support staff. 

The government encourages the involvement of youth in Tiatr productions to ensure the continuity of this cultural form. 

In addition to financial support, the government also provides logistical assistance. 

This includes help with venue arrangements and promotion of the productions. 

The scheme aligns with the broader cultural policies of the Government of Goa aimed at preserving local traditions. 

It also supports the vision of making Goa a cultural hub for performing arts in India. 

The government has plans to expand the scheme in the coming years. 

Future expansions may include increased funding and additional training programs for artists. 

The scheme is part of a larger initiative to promote various forms of art and culture in Goa. 

Overall, the "Production of Tiatr in Villages/Urban Areas/Educational Institutions" scheme is a significant step towards preserving and promoting the rich cultural heritage of Goa. 

It provides a structured approach to support local artists and ensures that Tiatr continues to thrive in the modern era. 

The initiative reflects the commitment of the Government of Goa to foster creativity and cultural expression among its citizens. 

As of October 2023, the scheme continues to be active and is receiving applications for new productions. 

This ongoing support is crucial for the sustenance of Tiatr as a vibrant part of Goan culture. 

The scheme not only benefits artists but also enriches the cultural landscape of the state. 

It is a testament to the importance of arts in community building and social cohesion. 

The government remains dedicated to enhancing the visibility and appreciation of Tiatr among younger generations. 

Through this scheme, the legacy of Tiatr is preserved for future audiences and performers alike.
